# pyproject.toml Checker: will my Python package build, install and upload?

> Free pyproject.toml checker. Reads the file and reports, with the line and a fix, what setuptools, hatchling or flit_core will refuse to build, what pip will not install and what PyPI will reject: TOML errors, unknown [project] keys (with the intended key), invalid PEP 440 versions and local versions, dynamic clashes, readme and content-type problems, PEP 639 license expressions (SPDX 3.27), the License :: classifier conflict (named per backend), license-files patterns, PEP 508 dependency strings (Poetry ^ syntax, direct URLs, marker values like sys_platform == 'windows' that are never true, extra markers in main dependencies), requires-python upper caps, unknown or deprecated trove classifiers, PEP 685 extras, PEP 735 dependency groups and cycles, a build-backend that build-system.requires never installs, and script entry points without a callable. Also previews the core metadata a backend writes. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded. A zero-dependency CLI has a CI exit code.

Free and open source (MIT). The TOML reader agrees with Python's tomllib on all 717 TOML 1.0 cases of toml-test; the version, specifier, requirement and SPDX grammars agree with packaging 26.3 on 16,000 generated strings; backend claims come from building test projects with setuptools 84.2.1, hatchling 1.33.0 and flit_core 4.2.0. Not legal or professional advice; a real build and upload is the final word.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/pyproject-metadata-check/)
- [Why license = "MIT License" breaks your Python build (PEP 639, measured per backend)](https://marisstella.app/pyproject-metadata-check/why-license-mit-license-breaks-your-build.html)

## For agents

- Engine: `engine.mjs`. `analyze(text, { files })` or `analyze({ text, files })`: `text` is the pyproject.toml, `files` an optional array of paths relative to it (for readme and license-files). Returns `ok` (no high finding), `findings` (severity high/medium/low/info, `id`, `line`, `path`, `message`, `fix`), `totals`, `summary` (name, version, backend, requiresPython, license, dependencies, extras) and `metadata` (core metadata preview, `fields` and `text`). Grammars in `pep.mjs`: `parseVersion`, `parseSpecifierSet`, `parseRequirement`, `parseLicenseExpression`. TOML: `toml.mjs` `parseToml` (values plus line numbers). Callable through `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call pyproject-metadata-check analyze --input '{"text":"[project]\nname = \"x\"\nversion = \"1\"\n"}'` or the repository's MCP server (`call_tool`).
- CLI: `node ventures/pyproject-metadata-check/cli.mjs [folder] [--json] [--metadata] [--fail-on high|medium|low|info|none] [--no-files]`.
